business.text: Avenue Supermarts Limited operates a national supermarket chain focusing on value-retailing across multiple product categories through brick-and-mortar stores [0.0, 3.12]. The company primarily runs on a cash and carry business model where it sells directly to customers [0.12]. It also operates the DMart Ready e-commerce platform [3.12].

cites.quote: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.
The group operates on business model of primarily cash and carry and credit risk from receivable perspective is not significant.
Notwithstanding the opportunities that are available in DMart Ready. We do that too. But it is not either / or. I keep saying brick-and-mortar and e-commerce is the way to go.

narrative.text: Both the annual reports and recent management calls emphasize Avenue Supermarts' focus on expanding its physical retail footprint and value-retailing model. While the annual report highlights operational metrics like employee counts and cash flows as of March 31, 2026 [0.2, 0.7], recent calls provide broader context on store additions, such as noting that 15 out of 85 stores opened last fiscal were leased [1.8] and mentioning an internal benchmark to grow the store base by around 15% annually [1.0].

bull.text: High ownership of properties provides operational stability, with the company owning approximately 88% of its properties.

cites.quote: if 88% (inadvertently mentioned as 92% on the audio call) of my property is ownership, we take a call on what money this location will make basis what we are going to invest in that store.

bull.point: High ownership of properties provides operational stability, with the company owning approximately 88% of its properties.

bull.text: The e-commerce business DMart Ready continues to experience solid growth rates.

cites.quote: Now, we have delivered a 21% or 22% growth rate vis-a-vis last year, purely on the DMart Ready business.

bull.point: The e-commerce business DMart Ready continues to experience solid growth rates.

bear.text: The e-commerce subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce continues to generate net losses.

cites.quote: Avenue E-Commerce grew sales by about 21% and the loss slightly widened to about 7%, the loss was at INR247 crores.
Avenue E-commerce delivered a 31.7% sales increase, close to INR2,900 crores and we had a loss of INR185 crores, which was a 240 bps loss reduction over the prior year.

bear.point: The e-commerce subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce continues to generate net losses.

bear.text: The company experienced rapid inflation on warehousing rentals and employee wages in the non-store area.

cites.quote: Second is in the non-store area, we found that there has been a rapid inflation on warehousing, whether it is warehousing rentals, warehousing employees, there has been unprecedented inflation in wages there.

bear.point: The company experienced rapid inflation on warehousing rentals and employee wages in the non-store area.

bear.text: Avenue Supermarts has previously had to significantly restructure or shut down portions of its DMart Ready pickup network locations.

cites.quote: Percy, we had 573 last year. There are 341 this year, we shut down 232.

bear.point: Avenue Supermarts has previously had to significantly restructure or shut down portions of its DMart Ready pickup network locations.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table provides only financial metrics such as revenue and operating profit, which cannot measure qualitative efforts regarding personal time spent on store expansion in North India.
promised.claim: Management plans to put disproportionate time personally into accelerating store expansion in North India over the next six to eight months.
promised.target: accelerate store expansion in North India
promised.quote: If you want to accelerate store expansion, which probably over the next six months to eight months, I'm going to put disproportionate time personally also, because North of India is what I'm going to handle from a real estate standpoint.

promised.evidence: The target horizon of a couple of years from August 2025 has not fully elapsed relative to the available table data, and the table does not provide specific segment profitability for DMart Ready.
promised.claim: Management expects DMart Ready to potentially break even in a couple of years.
promised.quote: So that's broadly what we feel about this.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not report store count figures to measure whether store openings reached at least 50.
promised.claim: Management states that store openings for the next year will not be less than 50.
promised.quote: I mean, it won't be less than 50. I mean, if you're talking so much about it.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table reports financial results and does not track online order delivery times for DMart Ready.
promised.claim: DMart Ready's vision is to deliver almost all online orders in six hours.
promised.quote: Our vision is to deliver almost all our orders in six hours. And I think for the basket value, see, the DMart Ready shopper is not shopping for immediacy.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table provides OPM% (ranging from 6.4 to 8.1 across the relevant quarters) but does not report gross margins or profit margins explicitly capped by this long-term policy.
promised.claim: Management states that the company will not earn a margin of more than 15% or thereabouts.
promised.quote: We are very clear, we'll not earn more than 15% or thereabouts.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table contains no regional breakdown of store openings for Uttar Pradesh or Odisha.
promised.claim: Management expects to see more store openings in Uttar Pradesh compared to Odisha due to existing inventory and acquired locations.
promised.quote: Possible to do both states, but we'll see more stores in UP for obvious reasons. We have inventory there. We have acquired some locations there. So, you'll see that coming.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not provide general merchandise and apparel (GMA) contribution percentages.
promised.claim: Management expects general merchandise and apparel (GMA) to trend around the current run rate of about 23%.
promised.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not report total store counts or new store opening counts.
promised.claim: Management states that new store openings should typically account for 10% to 15% of the total store count.
promised.quote: I've been saying this repeatedly that typically 10% to 15% of my number count should be my new store opening, broadly.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not provide store opening counts to verify the projected 40 to 45 store openings for the year.
promised.claim: Management projects 40 to 45 store openings for the current year.
promised.quote: Like I said, for this year also, we have projected 40-45 stores.

promised.evidence: The three-year horizon for store opening ranges extends beyond the available quarters in the table.
promised.claim: Management projects a store opening range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.
promised.quote: So, you can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table contains only financial data and does not track delivery time metrics for DMart Ready.
promised.claim: Management states that around 40% to 45% of DMart Ready home deliveries happen within 12 hours.
promised.quote: I think around 40%-45% of our deliveries happen within 12 hours.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table reports financial results and does not track DMart Ready home delivery turnaround times.
promised.claim: Management states that about 86% of DMart Ready home deliveries happen within 24 hours.
promised.quote: And about 86% of our deliveries happen within 24 hours

promised.evidence: The quarterly table lists operating profit margins (OPM%) such as 7.6 in Sep 2024 and 7.1 in Sep 2026, but does not report gross margins.
promised.claim: Management expects gross margins to play around 14% to 15%.
promised.quote: See, whatever we do today, 14%-15% gross margin, we're going to play around that.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table reports OPM% and trailing-four-quarter OPM% values, but does not provide blended gross margin figures.
promised.claim: Management expects blended average gross margins to remain within the range of 14.5%, 15%, and 15.5%.
promised.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint. You have to look at a blended gross margin.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table provides financial data and does not track the construction of fulfilment centres or delivery times.
promised.claim: Management aims to build fulfilment centres in large towns quickly to enable deliveries within 12 hours for DMart Ready.
promised.quote: We should do whatever it takes to build fulfilment centres in large towns quickly, as quickly as possible so that we are able to deliver in at least 12 hours. I mean, that's the aspiration.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not provide general merchandise and apparel (GMA) contribution metrics for FY 2024 or FY 2025.

promised.target: Equal to or better than FY24 GMA contribution
promised.quote: With a reasonable confidence, I can say that, this financial year will be equal to or better than FY '24 GMA contribution.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table does not contain apparel contribution percentages or pre-COVID baseline metrics.
promised.claim: Management believes apparel contribution can return to pre-COVID levels.
promised.quote: The way to look at it, Amit, is apparel we believe we can go back to the older days of contribution, which was maybe pre-COVID.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table reports revenue and net profit figures but does not report CAGR growth rates or store opening counts.
promised.claim: Management notes it is getting more challenging to maintain a 15% to 20% CAGR growth rate at only 40 stores per annum.
promised.quote: it is getting more and more challenging to maintain a 15% to 20% CAGR growth rate if I continue to grow at only 40 stores per annum.

promised.evidence: The quarterly table provides only high-level financial metrics and does not track the category scaling or store placement of pharmacies.
promised.claim: Management plans to scale up the pharmacy category and have it in as many stores as possible over a reasonable amount of time.
promised.quote: it will take us a reasonable amount of time to scale this up and have them in as many stores as possible.

promised.quote: we do see opportunities of going to Orissa, going to Uttar Pradesh (UP) and you will see some stores coming up in UP. We have already tied up a few firm deals in these states.

promised.quote: pharmacy takes around 600, 800, or sometimes even 300 square feet. So, a very small space.
